review_candidates.title: Senior Partnership Officer
review_candidates.description: The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future. CONTEXTUAL BACKGROUND In 2007, the IRC began providing humanitarian assistance to vulnerable and crisis-affected people in Jordan in response to an influx of Iraqi refugees and the strain on host communities. Following the eruption of the Syrian war in 2011, hundreds of thousands of refugees crossed into Jordan. The ongoing insecurity in Syria and the growing needs of refugees have strained Jordan’s resources and infrastructure and exacerbated pre-existing issues like water scarcity and high unemployment. As resources become more limited, refugees and host communities have fewer economic opportunities and become more vulnerable. The IRC’s strategy for Jordan shows our commitment to improving the safety, health, education, and economic well-being of people affected by conflict, in camp-based refugees and urban-based refugees as well as vulnerable Jordanian host community, in coordination with the humanitarian community and the Government of Jordan. Simultaneously, IRC in Jordan is pivoting to a more long-term resilience/development programming responding to the context in Jordan and the worsening vulnerabilities faced by refugees and vulnerable Jordanians. SCOPE OF WORK The Senior Partnerships Officer supports the growth and quality of partnerships within the IRC Jordan Country Program. The post contributes to identifying, building, and sustaining strategic partnerships with government actors, civil society organizations, women-led and women-focused organizations, community-based organizations, and private sector actors, and coordinates the day-to-day partnership lifecycle, including support to the sub-awards portfolio, so that every partnership is effective, well organized, and compliant with IRC and donor requirements. The post contributes to the Country Program’s commitment to move progressively from direct service delivery toward partnerships, systems strengthening, and advocacy that improve sustainable access for the most vulnerable. Jordan’s service landscape is actor-rich but pathway-poor, and local organizations remain under-resourced and insufficiently integrated into coordination, referral, and decision-making. The Senior Partnerships Officer helps close that gap by supporting the expansion and diversification of the partnership ecosystem, promoting equitable co-design and co-delivery with local actors, supporting partner capacity strengthening, and contributing to the case across the Country Program for partnership as the route to reach, quality, and sustainability. The post works under the guidance of the Senior Programs Coordinator and collaborates with program, technical, finance, compliance, and MEAL teams to apply partnership principles consistently, promote positive and respectful ways of working with partners, and contribute to integrated, multi-sectoral service delivery across health, education, safety, and economic recovery and development. Major Responsibilities Strategic partnership development and localization Maintain and regularly update a partnership ecosystem map and stakeholder analysis covering government, civil society organizations, youth and women-led and women-focused organizations, OPDs, community-based actors, and private sector actors, identifying where partnership can strengthen access, referral pathways, and local reach. Support the development and maintenance of a prioritized pipeline of prospective strategic partners aligned with the Strategy Action Plan priorities and priority geographies, and provide analysis and recommendations to the Senior Programs Coordinator. Support targeted outreach, networking, exposure visits, and relationship-building with prospective partners to establish trust, shared priorities, and long-term collaboration. Support structured relationship management with strategic partners, including coordination with designated relationship managers, preparation for regular senior leadership alignment meetings, and the annual partnership health check to assess performance and strengthen collaboration. Contribute to equitable co-design and co-delivery by supporting the engagement of community-based organizations, women-led organizations, and other local actors from program design through implementation, so that approaches are community-rooted and locally relevant. Support business development with partners by identifying joint funding opportunities, coordinating partner inputs to concept notes and proposals, and contributing to engagement strategies for diversified financing, including private sector, CSR, and philanthropic sources. Advocate internally for a partnership-first approach in program design and proposal development, and contribute to strategic planning discussions, providing teams with analysis, tools, and examples that show how partnership improves reach, quality, cost-efficiency, and sustainability. Support the capacity-sharing agenda with partners, working with technical and operational teams to identify two-way learning and institutional strengthening opportunities, and to support a greater role for local actors in decision-making, delivery, and representation. Track and report progress against Country Program partnership commitments, including the share of the Country Program budget channeled to local partners, the number of strategic partnerships developed, and the number of those that are women-led or women-focused, and flag risks and opportunities to the Senior Programs Coordinator. Capture and share evidence and lessons from partnerships to support IRC Jordan’s learning agenda and to inform future partnership choices. Partnership lifecycle management Design phase Screen the prospective partners list and conduct basic stakeholder analysis and social network analysis. Schedule and lead meetings with prospective partners and complete the organizational snapshot tool. Schedule design meetings with selected partners, applying a partnership-first lens that prioritizes local actors, including community-based and women-led organizations, where appropriate. Collect partners’ documents and file them properly in the system. Support the development of partners’ scope of work and the government approval cover letter. Prepare the teaming agreement or Pre-Award Letter (PAL) with partners for review and signature by the authorized IRC signatory. Organize and conduct the Partner Capacity Analysis (PCA) in coordination with other IRC units, using the findings to identify capacity-sharing opportunities as well as risks. Consolidate IRC scoring based on the information collected. Facilitate the development of the Project Support Plan based on findings, with input from relevant teams. Planning and start-up phase Draft the Partnership Agreement with all annexes, in collaboration with compliance, programs, and finance, and share it with all relevant teams for comments before initiating the workflow on OTIS. Program implementation phase Schedule the opening meeting with partners, develop and deliver the Partners’ Project Opening Meeting (PPOM) presentation, and prepare the minutes of meeting (MoM). Support the application of the GEDI Marker at the project opening meeting to review safety, inclusion, access barriers, and follow-up actions with partners. Share all reporting templates with partners. Schedule, coordinate, and document partner monitoring visits and meetings, using them for joint problem-solving and capacity sharing as well as compliance. Follow up with partners on regular reports. Coordinate the review of partners’ financial and technical reports, ensuring full alignment between both, and provide feedback to partners for reflection. Request, collect, review, and archive supporting documents. Schedule, conduct, and document reflection meetings with partners when needed. Learning and closeout phase Collect partners’ feedback forms. Schedule and document the closing meeting with partners and programs, and contribute to assessing which partnerships are suitable to deepen or transition into longer-term or strategic relationships. Draft the closure letter for the Country Director’s signature and share it with partners. Ensure final reports and closing documents are complete and properly filed. Provide the certificate of closure to partners. Draft the partnership project review memorandum, secure the Country Director’s signature, and share it with the partner. Prepare the government progress report and the project closeout cover letters with partners. Coordination, compliance, and reporting Provide contextual research and analysis to inform partnership choices and business development. Track sub-awards and partner budgets in coordination with Finance and flag issues early to the Senior Programs Coordinator. Support partnership compliance with IRC policies and donor requirements, including safeguarding, protection from sexual exploitation and abuse, fiscal integrity, and anti-retaliation standards, and escalate concerns promptly. Maintain accurate, accessible partnership records, trackers, and filing systems. Prepare partnership-related reports for internal and donor audiences as requested. Maintain effective working-level relationships with partners, coordination bodies, and other stakeholders. General Promote and actively participate in initiatives and efforts to build team engagement, inclusion, and cohesion in the IRC Jordan office. Foster ongoing learning, honest dialogue, and reflection to strengthen safeguarding and to promote IRC values and adherence to IRC policies. Perform any other related duties as assigned by the supervisor. KEY WORKING RELATIONSHIPS Position reports to: Senior Programs Coordinator Position directly supervises: N/A Key external stakeholders: Government ministries and national coordinating bodies, municipalities, UN agencies, INGOs, national NGOs, community-based organizations, civil society organizations, women-led and women-focused organizations, feminist organizations, private sector companies and foundations, and donors. Job Requirements Work experience: Minimum of 5 years’ experience in partnerships, business development, or program roles with INGOs or national NGOs, including demonstrated experience building and managing partnerships with local organizations. Demonstrated Skills And Competencies Demonstrated ability to contribute to building and sustaining partnerships with diverse actors, including government, civil society, community-based organizations, and private sector entities. Sound knowledge of the partnership lifecycle, including partner due diligence, capacity assessment, sub-award management, and donor compliance requirements. Understanding of localization and equitable partnership principles, including co-design, co-delivery, and capacity sharing. Good stakeholder analysis and relationship management skills, with the ability to work collaboratively across teams and with external partners. Ability to contribute to business development, including identifying funding opportunities and coordinating partner inputs to proposals. Strong organizational, analytical, and reporting skills, with high attention to detail and the ability to manage multiple partnerships at once. Excellent written and verbal communication skills. Good ICT skills, including MS Word, MS Excel, MS PowerPoint, and online survey tools. Preferred Qualifications Experience working with women-led or women-focused organizations, feminist organizations, or community-based organizations. Experience engaging private sector, CSR, or philanthropic actors. Familiarity with the humanitarian and development context in Jordan and with government coordination structures. Knowledge of gender equality, disability, and social inclusion approaches. Language Language: Strong English and Arabic language skills are required. WORKING ENVIRONMENT This position is based in Amman, with frequent travel to IRC program sites and partner locations in Jordan. The security situation in the IRC intervention areas is calm, and the security department of IRC shares regular security updates to keep the management and staff informed about the new developments. Professional Standards: All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct. Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on Safeguarding, Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients. review_candidates.description: Background JOB DESCRIPTION UN Women, grounded in the vision of equality enshrined in the Charter of the United Nations, works for the elimination of discrimination against women and girls; the empowerment of women; and the achievement of equality between women and men as partners and beneficiaries of development, human rights, humanitarian action and peace and security. UN Women has been providing continues support to partners in the South Caucasus to increase meaningful participation of women in peace and security processes. Under the current country program and in line with UN Sustainable Development Cooperation Framework (UNSDCF) 2026 – 2030 in Armenia, UN Women supports the Government of Armenia to develop and implement National Action Plans for the implementation of UN Security Council Resolutions on Women, Peace, and Security #1325 (2000) et al. and to achieve targets of the nationalized SDG 5 and 16. UN Women in Armenia, with funding support from the UK Government, the Swedish International Development Cooperation Agency, and the Government of Denmark, is implementing initiatives aimed at enhancing women’s full, equal, direct and meaningful participation in peace and security processes and strengthening the capacities of state and non-state actors to advance the Women, Peace and Security (WPS) agenda in Armenia and fulfil commitments undertaken at the international, regional and national levels. Reporting to the Programme Specialists based in Yerevan, Armenia, under the overall guidance of the UN Women Country Representative in Georgia and Liaison for the South Caucasus, the Programme Analyst contributes to the effective management and implementation of UN Women’s WPS interventions in Armenia by providing substantive technical support to programme design, implementation, monitoring, evaluation, and reporting. The Programme Analyst will lead policy dialogue, advocacy, capacity development, and inter-agency coordination to advance the implementation of the WPS agenda in Armenia. The position develops and maintains strategic partnerships with government institutions, civil society organizations, academia, think tanks, development partners, donors, and the United Nations system, while contributing to resource mobilization and the expansion of the WPS work in Armenia. Working in close collaboration with programme and operations teams in Armenia, the Georgia Country Office, and the Regional Office, the Programme Analyst ensures the effective delivery of the WPS portfolio in alignment with the UN Women Strategic Plan, the Armenia Biannual Work Plan, and national commitments under the WPS agenda. Provide substantive inputs to building partnerships and resource mobilization strategies Provide substantive inputs to resource mobilization strategies; analyze and maintain information and databases; Prepare relevant documentation such as project summaries, conference papers, briefing notes, speeches, and donor profiles; and Participate in donor meetings and public information events, as delegated. review_candidates.description: Product Owner Automated Production Wil jij een sleutelrol spelen in de ontwikkeling van een nieuw, geautomatiseerd productiesysteem? Voor een internationale technologieorganisatie in Eindhoven zoeken wij een ervaren Product Owner Automated Production. In deze functie ben je verantwoordelijk voor het ontwikkelen en realiseren van een geavanceerd productiesysteem waarin industriële automatisering, robotica en slimme productietechnologieën samenkomen. Je krijgt de mogelijkheid om vanaf de basis een technisch projectteam op te bouwen en de ontwikkeling van het productiesysteem vorm te geven. Van de eerste technische requirements en conceptontwikkeling tot de daadwerkelijke implementatie. Een uitdagende functie op het snijvlak van product ownership, technisch projectmanagement, industrial automation en robotisering. Jouw rol Als Product Owner ben je verantwoordelijk voor de ontwikkeling en implementatie van een nieuw, geautomatiseerd productiesysteem. Je vertaalt de behoeften vanuit de organisatie naar concrete technische en functionele requirements en ontwikkelt een heldere visie op de inrichting en werking van het systeem. Daarbij ben je niet alleen verantwoordelijk voor de productroadmap en prioriteiten, maar neem je ook de leiding in de technische realisatie. Je brengt engineers, automatiseringsspecialisten en externe leveranciers samen en zorgt ervoor dat de verschillende technologieën uiteindelijk één geïntegreerd productiesysteem vormen. Je belangrijkste verantwoordelijkheden: Opzetten en aansturen van een multidisciplinair technisch projectteam; Ontwikkelen van de visie, productroadmap en technische requirements voor het geautomatiseerde productiesysteem; Vertalen van productiebehoeften naar slimme automatiseringsoplossingen; Begeleiden van conceptontwikkeling, prototyping, engineering en testen; Definiëren van industriële automatiseringsprocessen en integreren van robotica; Coördineren van interne technische teams, stakeholders en externe leveranciers; Bewaken van planning, budget, kwaliteit en technische voortgang; Verantwoordelijkheid nemen voor de succesvolle implementatie en verdere optimalisatie van het productiesysteem. Wie zoeken wij? We zoeken een ervaren technische professional die complexe automatiseringsprojecten kan overzien en beschikt over de leiderschapskwaliteiten om deze daadwerkelijk te realiseren. Je beschikt over: Een afgeronde technische hbo- of wo-opleiding, bij voorkeur richting Robotics, Mechatronics, Industrial Automation of Systems Engineering; Minimaal 8 jaar relevante ervaring binnen technische productontwikkeling, industriële automatisering, robotisering of Manufacturing Execution Systems (MES); Minimaal 5 jaar ervaring met het leiden van omvangrijke technische projecten; Kennis van geautomatiseerde productieprocessen, industriële systemen en robotica; Sterke projectmanagementvaardigheden en ervaring met multidisciplinaire teams; Het vermogen om technische vraagstukken te vertalen naar praktische en schaalbare oplossingen; Uitstekende communicatieve vaardigheden en een gestructureerde manier van werken. Je beheerst het Nederlands op moedertaalniveau en spreekt daarnaast goed Engels (minimaal B2). Wat kun je verwachten? Je komt terecht bij een internationale technologieorganisatie waar innovatie en technische ontwikkeling centraal staan. Het bijzondere aan deze functie is dat je niet instapt in een bestaand productieproces, maar juist betrokken wordt bij het ontwikkelen en opbouwen van een nieuw geautomatiseerd productiesysteem. Je krijgt veel ruimte om technische keuzes te beïnvloeden, de juiste specialisten samen te brengen en de ontwikkeling van het systeem van begin tot eind te begeleiden. Daarnaast kun je rekenen op: Een aantrekkelijk arbeidsvoorwaardenpakket; Veel verantwoordelijkheid en ruimte voor eigen initiatief; Een moderne werkomgeving in Eindhoven; Mogelijkheden om hybride te werken; Een internationale, multidisciplinaire werkomgeving; Een informele bedrijfscultuur met korte communicatielijnen. Interesse? Heb jij ervaring met industrial automation, robotics of het ontwikkelen van geautomatiseerde productiesystemen? En lijkt het je interessant om vanaf de basis verantwoordelijk te zijn voor een nieuw technisch project? Dan komen we graag met je in contact. We vertellen je graag meer over de organisatie, de technische uitdagingen en de mogelijkheden binnen deze functie.
